title: scripts/ is excluded from lint and typecheck, so release tooling has no static analysis
description:
scripts/ is excluded from BOTH lint and typecheck, so every .mjs in it -- including release tooling that only executes during a release -- ships with zero static analysis.

MEASURED, not inferred:
  biome.json   files.includes = ["src/**/*.ts", "test/**/*.ts", "benchmark/**/*.ts", "*.json"]
  tsconfig.json  include       = ["src/**/*.ts", "test/**/*.ts", "benchmark/**/*.ts", "*.ts"]

Neither pattern matches scripts/. `bun run lint` reports only its one pre-existing src/ warning; `bun run typecheck` never opens the directory.

PROOF IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The LCLI-481 provenance gate (scripts/release-provenance.mjs, 560 lines) shipped a completely unused top-level ANNOTATION constant and CI was green. tsconfig already sets noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters to true -- both would have caught it had the file been in scope. Found by adversarial review, not by any gate.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN RECORD rather than part of LCLI-481: the gap is a property of the repository, not of that gate. Folded into LCLI-481 it would disappear when LCLI-481 closes, which is precisely how the next person rediscovers it. Orchestrator ruling, 2026-09-13. It must NOT gate the 0.6.2 release.

THE SHARP EDGE: this is the least-inspected code in the repository and it is also the code that runs during the one irreversible operation. scripts/ holds publish-release.sh (the manual publish path that 0.6.1 shipped through and 0.6.2 will), and release-provenance.mjs. A typo in either surfaces mid-release.

WORTH CHECKING WHILE HERE: whether the whole directory can be brought in at once or whether some files need scoped exclusions, and whether benchmark/ and any other top-level directory have the same hole.

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/**/*.mjs is covered by `bun run lint` (biome files.includes) and by `bun run typecheck` (tsconfig include), or any file that cannot be is excluded EXPLICITLY with a recorded reason rather than by the pattern silently missing it

The regression that proved the gap is caught: re-introducing an unused top-level constant in a scripts/ .mjs fails one of the two checks (noUnusedLocals is already enabled, so this should follow from the include alone -- verify it rather than assume it)
Any other top-level directory with the same hole is either brought in or named as deliberately excluded, so the answer is recorded rather than rediscovered
`bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` all pass, with no new warnings beyond the known pre-existing src/commands/agents.ts:216

comments.body:
IMPLEMENTATION WARNING, from the agent that caused this finding, 2026-09-13. The two halves of this task have very different costs and should probably be split.

BIOME HALF -- cheap, and it catches the exact defect that produced this record. Biome lints .mjs with no type information and no annotations required. Verified against a scratch file with biome 2.4.12:
    sample.mjs:1:7 lint/correctness/noUnusedVariables  This variable ANNOTATION is unused.
That is the dead constant that shipped green. Do this half first; it is nearly free.

TSC HALF -- NOT what AC#0 literally says, and the literal reading is a NO-OP. Adding scripts/**/*.mjs to tsconfig.json include WITHOUT allowJs does nothing whatsoever. Measured:
    error TS18003: No inputs were found in config file. Specified include paths were ["scripts/**/*.mjs"]
With --allowJs --checkJs it does check the file, and then demands JSDoc throughout: TS7006 on every untyped parameter, TS2339 on every property of a parsed JSON body (which is {} under strict). That applies to EVERY .mjs in scripts/, not just the one that prompted this.

So the honest shape is: biome now, tsc as a deliberate decision about whether release tooling is worth annotating. AC#0 as written implies both are the same edit. They are not. Re-read it before implementing rather than discovering this halfway.

NOTHING WAS CHANGED to learn this: the scratch tsconfig was created and deleted inside one command, and the biome sample lives outside the repo. biome.json and tsconfig.json are untouched on every branch.
